issues.description: The datasheet records a legally binding consent gate: response data may not be disclosed without participants' prior written consent. All nine named response exports are absent from the supplied package, and the package does not establish whether prior consent already authorizes release or whether a compliant author-prepared export is obtainable. This is an actual documented access condition, not a finding that consent was denied or that authorization is absent. Until an already-authorized response-level route is documented, the required exports remain blocked.

The full native scope includes Table 1, Table 4, and Figure 2, which the datasheet says were produced manually in Excel. The registered release has no workbook, underlying source materials, or manual calculation steps, so this manual producer stage is not closed. Classifying every frozen checklist ID does not supply the missing manual producer contract.

Three producer basenames differ from their consumer spellings only by the case of the final N/n: List1-LinkedIN/LinkedIn, List2-LinkedIN/LinkedIn, and DirectQ-LinkedIN/LinkedIn. Align the case in the working copies before running on a case-sensitive filesystem.

The supplied code uses literal DIRECTORY NAME/RAW DATA DIRECTORY NAME placeholders and its intended per-driver working roots and output mappings are not established. Treat these as ordinary path configuration; source-screen masking of separate path-setting blocks does not prove that a real private author path was supplied. Configure a coherent working copy without exposing withheld text or changing the original source files.

A local Compustat annual-file candidate is readable, but the required field mapping between revt and sale, SIC field semantics, target-firm key crosswalk, and latest-fiscal-year selection/coverage are not specified or verified.

The author-collected random-500 firm identities, founding-decade records, supporting sources, and firm-to-target-sample crosswalk are not in the release. Static SEC/Yahoo pages establish only candidate source categories, not the needed records or coverage.
Both authored design-effect branches require kict deff, and the exact kict command is unavailable in the metadata-only which probe.
The required manual Excel branch is documented, but an Excel runtime and version have not been verified on the host.

evidence.description: The datasheet identifies the three supplied Stata programs and their stated roles.
evidence.quote:
The three sets of Stata code file contain the required codes to convert different sets of raw
Qualtrics data described in Item 2 above into the final datasets used in the analysis and to
produce the results presented in the paper. “List Experiment” converts the raw Qualtrics data
and produces the list experiment results presented in Tables 3, 5, OA1, and OA2. “Survey”
converts the raw Qualtrics data and produces the direct questioning survey results presented in
Tables 3, 5, and OA2. “Demographics” combines the list experiment and direct survey raw
data and tabulates various descriptive statistics, including those presented in Table 2. The MS
Word file “Stata Code Execution Log” contains the execution logs for all three sets of Stata

review_notes: The assessed target is the full author-documented pipeline. All three supplied Stata drivers and all 25 frozen checklist IDs remain represented, but `closure_complete` is false because the required manual Excel producer for Tables 1 and 4 and Figure 2 lacks its workbook/source materials and calculation steps. Checklist coverage alone does not close that native stage.

The nine response workbooks remain separate inputs. The datasheet states an actual prior-written-consent condition on disclosure; the route is blocked pending evidence that existing consent permits the needed disclosure. The package does not establish whether consent exists or has been denied, nor whether an authorized export is obtainable. No respondent contact or request for new consent was made or proposed; no new data were collected or reconstructed.
Tables 1 and 4 and Figure 2 are separate manual Excel outputs. The source workbook/materials and manual recipe are absent, and Excel availability is unverified.

Table 2 column 5 has two jointly required, separate constructions: Compustat SIC/revenue from each target firm's latest fiscal year, and founding decade for an author-selected random 500 target firms. A local Compustat candidate was read only through a bounded one-row metadata probe; the exact revenue field, SIC semantics, firm key, year-selection/history, and population coverage remain unknown. The random-500 identity/crosswalk and source records are also absent. SEC/Yahoo pages are unverified candidates only; no external company payloads were retrieved.

The code uses Aware in missing-value statements while other stages retain Awareness. Aware could be a unique abbreviation of Awareness if Stata's imported namespace and varabbrev setting permit it; this is neither a proven alias nor a supported missing-variable finding. No rename is proposed.

Both authored kict deff calls remain required. The second keeps the source's set obs 1577 and designated observation values; this author-specified design-effect test was preserved without a runtime trial or methodological repair.

Three case-only staged-file mismatches remain proposed as exact working-copy basename edits. Literal directory placeholder strings are visible in import statements; treat them as ordinary path configuration, and do not infer that conservative screening of separate path-setting blocks proves a real private path. No author source was edited or executed, and raw startup/software logs remain opaque.
Available Stata and command claims use metadata-only probes. Excel remains unverified, and kict is unavailable in the exact which-only check. The final assessment does not claim execution success.
